Welcome to
Elizabeth Selby Infants' School
Governors
The Governing Body at Elizabeth Selby Infant School works in partnership with the Headteacher and staff to ensure the school provides the best possible education for all children.
Governors are volunteers who help the school by providing strategic oversight, support, and challenge. They are not involved in day-to-day management.
What Governors Do
Set the school’s strategic direction
Oversee financial performance and resource management
Governing Body Structure
Our governing body includes:
Co-opted Governors
Parent Governors
Local Authority Governors
Staff Governors
Associate Members (non-voting)
Current Governors
Richard Ellis – Chair of Governors (Co-opted)
Richard leads the governing body and ensures governors work effectively together. He has experience in school leadership and governance and focuses on strategic planning, accountability, and school improvement.
Oliver Hopwood – Vice Chair / Safeguarding Governor (Local Authority)
Oliver supports the Chair and takes a lead role in safeguarding oversight. He ensures safeguarding policies and procedures are robust, regularly reviewed, and effectively implemented.
Shahi Ahmed – Headteacher (Staff Governor)
Shahi provides the governing body with insight into day-to-day school leadership and improvement priorities. He works closely with governors to implement the school’s vision and development plan.
Abu Forhad – Parent Governor
Abu brings a parent perspective to the governing body, helping ensure decisions reflect the needs of families and pupils. He supports communication between parents and the school.
Rayhan Uddin – Parent Governor
Rayhan contributes a strong understanding of the school community and supports governors in reviewing school policies and outcomes from a parent viewpoint.
Elijah Marshall – Co-opted Governor
Elijah supports the governing body with a focus on school improvement and accountability. He brings external experience to help challenge and support leadership decisions.
Jazpreet Rana-Patel – Co-opted Governor
Jazpreet contributes experience in community engagement and organisational development, helping the governing body consider wider community impact and inclusion.
Karen Breen – Associate Member (Staff)
Karen supports the governing body by contributing operational and staff-level insight. She is not a voting member but provides valuable information to support decision-making.
Key Roles
Chair of GovernorsProvides leadership to the governing body and ensures effective governance, accountability, and strategic direction.
Safeguarding Governor
Leads oversight of safeguarding arrangements, ensuring all policies and procedures keep children safe.
Headteacher Governor
Provides operational insight and works closely with governors to implement school priorities.
Guidance for Parent Governors
Paper copies of minutes can be made available if and when required. Please contact our admin team on 0207 739 6187 or email at admin@elizabethselby.towerhamlets.sch.uk
For more information please contact 020 7364 3141 or email Governor.servicessection@towerhamlets.gov.uk

Elizabeth Selby Infants' School
Welcome to
Elizabeth Selby Infants' School
Early Learning for 2 Year Olds
At Elizabeth Selby Infant School, we believe that young children learn best through play and by following their own interests and fascinations. Our curriculum is rich, varied, and carefully planned to provide stimulating experiences that encourage curiosity, exploration, and early learning, both indoors and in our dedicated outdoor space for two-year-olds.
Our Seedling Class focuses on helping children become confident, independent learners who are able to make choices for themselves while developing a caring and respectful attitude towards others and their environment. We recognise the importance of consistency, and the regular routines, familiar adults, and stable peer group all play a key role in supporting children’s early development and wellbeing.
In Seedlings, staff place a strong emphasis on the prime areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage: communication and language, personal, social and emotional development, and physical development. These are developed through high-quality interactions during free-flow play as well as short, focused group sessions.
Please click here for a Early Learning for 2 Year Old Application

Breakfast Club
Elizabeth Selby Breakfast Club provides a safe, welcoming, and fun environment for children to start their school day. The club is free of charge and open to all pupils. It offers a calm and supportive space where children can enjoy breakfast, socialise, and take part in relaxed activities before lessons begin.
We aim to meet the needs of all children. If your child has special educational needs or disabilities and requires additional support, please speak to a member of the Breakfast Club staff so we can ensure the right arrangements are in place.

Each morning, children can choose from a range of activities, including:
The aim is for children to feel settled, happy, and ready to learn when they go to class.

Structured games and activities

A nutritious breakfast is provided each day, and children are encouraged to sit together, enjoy their food, and clear away afterwards to support independence and social skills.
We offer a variety of options, including:

pageCache.text:
Elizabeth Selby Infants' School
Welcome to
Elizabeth Selby Infants' School
Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education
At Elizabeth Selby Infant School, we believe PSHE is at the heart of children’s personal development and wellbeing. Through our PSHE curriculum, we aim to support children to become confident, respectful, resilient and caring individuals who are able to build positive relationships, understand their emotions and make safe and healthy choices.
Using the Jigsaw PSHE scheme, we provide children with the knowledge, skills and understanding they need to thrive both in school and in the wider world. We encourage children to value themselves and others, celebrate diversity and develop the confidence to contribute positively to their community and society.
In EYFS, PSHE is primarily taught through the Early Years Foundation Stage area of learning “Personal, Social and Emotional Development.” Children are supported to build positive relationships, develop self-confidence and learn how to understand and manage their feelings and behaviour.
Children learn through play, daily routines, stories, circle times and practical experiences. They are encouraged to share, take turns, cooperate with others and develop friendships. Adults carefully support children in recognising emotions, solving problems and developing resilience and independence.
Through the Jigsaw approach and wider classroom experiences, children begin to understand how to keep themselves healthy and safe, respect others and develop confidence in their own abilities. Activities help children to build communication skills, empathy and an understanding of classroom expectations and routines.
Children also learn through wider opportunities including assemblies, community projects, visits, role play and discussions. Our nurturing environment supports children to feel valued, included and confident as learners.
Wider PSHE Opportunities
At Elizabeth Selby Infant School, PSHE extends beyond dedicated lessons and is embedded throughout school life. Children develop their understanding of relationships, wellbeing and citizenship through assemblies, class discussions, visits, themed events and community partnerships.
We promote a strong culture of emotional wellbeing through approaches such as Zones of Regulation and Growth Mindset language, helping children to recognise emotions, build resilience and develop positive attitudes towards learning.
Children also benefit from opportunities to engage with the wider community through local projects, visitors and partnerships, helping them to develop empathy, responsibility and an understanding of the world around them.
Elizabeth Selby Infants' School

Welcome to

Headteacher's Message
Thank you for your interest in our school and welcome to our website!
As a parent, your child is the most important thing in your life and choosing the right school is one of the most important decisions you will make.
At Elizabeth Selby we have children aged from 2 to 7 years. For their junior education the children move to our partner school next door – Lawdale Juniors and remain very much a part of our school community.
We are an Infant school that is passionate about early education. We offer the children a warm and nurturing environment as we understand that children who feel safe, valued and cared for will be in the best position to learn.
We are a Rights Respecting School and this is reflected in how the children and staff go about their day. We deliver a curriculum that is exciting as well as challenging and is tailored to the needs of the children.
We believe in strong partnerships with parents and encourage our parents to regularly engage with us about their children’s learning and become part of our school community.Children achieve well in our school and we have very strong academic results. Above all, we aim to develop happy, well rounded, capable children who are well prepared for the next stage of their lives.
I hope you enjoy looking at our website.
Best WishesShahi Ahmed

Welcome to
Elizabeth Selby Infants' School
SEND Offer
School SENCO: Joe Howard
At Elizabeth Selby Infant School, we are committed to ensuring that all children, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), are fully included, supported, and able to access all areas of school life.
We follow the SEND Code of Practice (2014) and ensure that children and parents are actively involved in all discussions and decisions relating to individual support and provision. The needs of each child are always at the centre of our planning and decision-making.
If you are worried about your child’s development or learning, please speak in the first instance to your child’s class teacher. They will be able to arrange a meeting with relevant staff, including the SENCO if appropriate.
We are committed to equality of opportunity and inclusion for all pupils. Our aim is to ensure that all learning is accessible, regardless of individual needs or disabilities. Children are encouraged to respect and support one another, and to value differences within our school community.
The Local Offer – London Borough of Tower Hamlets
The Local Offer – London Borough of Tower Hamlets
Families can access information, advice, and support about SEND through the Tower Hamlets Local Offer, which provides details of services and provision available locally.
link to accessibility plan
SEN Information Report
Our sensory room provides a calm, safe, and stimulating environment designed to support children’s sensory development and emotional regulation. It includes a range of sensory experiences such as lights, colours, sounds, and soft play equipment, allowing children to explore and engage in a supportive setting tailored to their needs.
Elizabeth Selby Infant School proudly offers two specialist autism classes: Chestnut Class and Hazel Class.
In partnership with Phoenix School, we use the Phoenix Steps framework alongside the SCERTS Model to assess, support, and guide children’s progress.
This structured pathway allows children to progress from Chestnut to Hazel Class where appropriate, ensuring continuity, consistency, and tailored support at every stage.
Both classes provide highly specialised teaching and intervention, including sensory stories, speech and language therapy, music therapy, sensory circuits, swimming therapy, and more.
With additional funding from Tower Hamlets and regular support from the Phoenix Outreach Team, we are able to maintain a high-quality, nurturing environment where children make strong and meaningful progress.

Admissions
At Elizabeth Selby Infant School, we welcome applications for children aged 2 to 7 years. As an infant school, we provide a nurturing and supportive environment where children are given the best possible start to their education.
The policy and arrangements for admission to the school are set out in the Local Authority's school admissions booklet “Starting School in Tower Hamlets”, which can be accessed at www.towerhamlets.gov.uk/schooladmissions. A paper copy can be obtained from the Local Authority's Pupil Admissions Team on 020 7364 5006.
Admissions to the school are managed by the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, and all applications should be made through the local authority admissions process. Places are allocated in line with the council’s published admissions criteria.
We encourage prospective parents and carers to visit the school and contact the office if they would like further information or support with the admissions process. We are always happy to help guide families through the next steps.
For more information about Free School Meals and to check eligibility, please complete the form below:

To help us support your child and family from the very beginning, we ask all parents and carers to complete the admission forms below and return them to the school office as soon as possible. These forms provide important information about your child’s health, development, emergency contacts, and any additional support they may require.
Please ensure that all sections are completed accurately and that any requested documentation is provided. If you need assistance completing any of the forms, our office team will be happy to help.
The following admission forms can be downloaded below:
Completed forms can be returned to the school office in person or by email. If you require printed copies of any of the forms, please contact the school office and we will be happy to provide them.

Art/Design Technology
At our infant school, Art and Design Technology are recognised as fundamental to fostering creativity, imagination and self-expression. Our inclusive curriculum provides opportunities for pupils to explore ideas, experiment with a range of materials and develop confidence in their creative abilities. Pupils engage in drawing, painting, designing, making and evaluating, enabling them to think critically, solve problems and take pride in their work. Through the study of artists, designers and craftspeople from diverse cultures, pupils develop cultural awareness and an appreciation of creativity in its many forms. We aim to develop confident, curious and imaginative learners who demonstrate enthusiasm, resilience and independence when responding to creative challenges.
In the Early Years Foundation Stage, Art and Design Technology is taught through play-based and exploratory experiences that develop children’s creativity, imagination and early expressive skills. Provision is planned in line with the Early Years Foundation Stage Framework (Expressive Arts and Design) and includes both continuous provision and adult-led activities.

Welcome to
Elizabeth Selby Infants' School
Computing
At Elizabeth Selby Infant School we have a clear and simple vision: the children should be online-safe, online-inspired and online-confident
At Elizabeth Selby Infant School, our aim is to prepare our learners for their future by giving them opportunities to gain knowledge and develop skills that will equip them for an ever changing digital world. We want all our pupils to be competent in the key areas of computing and ICT and able to apply their knowledge and understanding safely in real-life and ever changing situations. Knowledge and understanding of ICT is of increasing importance for our children’s future both at home and for employment.
Teach Computing focuses on a progression of skills in digital literacy, computer science, information technology and online safety to ensure that children become competent in safely using, as well as understanding, technology. In computer science we will teach the principles of information and computation, how digital systems work and how to put this knowledge to use through programming information. In addition, we aim to ensure our children are equipped to use information technology to create programs, systems and a range of content. Computing also ensures that our pupils become digitally literate – able to explore, use, and express themselves and develop their ideas through, information and communication technology – at a level suitable for the future workplace and as active participants in a digital world. We supplement Teach Computing with resources from Project Evolve to support Online Safety.
The goal of Teach Computing is to transform the way computing is taught in schools across the country – and enable more young people to benefit from studying this important subject. Through this, their skills and career opportunities will be enhanced in the future.
Below is the curriculum journey our computing will follow from EYFS to Year 2. The framework uses an innovative progression to allow to children to build on their prior learning year on year. Each year group will have a unit of work linked to each of the following areas:
At Elizabeth Selby Infants, our pupils have access to a variety of digital devices which are used to support teaching across the curriculum. We have interactive screens in every classroom, a class set of iPads, a computer suite with 15 computers, Chromebooks, data loggers, programmable toys, and other devices to help children apply their skills.
By the end of the curriculum, the...
Our pupils learn about the key aspects of computing (digital literacy, information technology, and computer science) through a variety of units that provide them with key skills that will serve them now and in later life.
Computing systems and networks
Data and information
Programming (A and B).

Elizabeth Selby Infants' School
Welcome to
Elizabeth Selby Infants' School
English
English at Elizabeth Selby Infant School
At Elizabeth Selby Infant School, English sits at the heart of our curriculum – it is through language, story and text that children learn to form concepts, connect ideas and express themselves. We strive to develop a love for the English language in its written and spoken forms. We encourage children to develop the skills to communicate confidently and effectively in speaking and writing. Children learn to listen with understanding and to be responsive, enthusiastic, knowledgeable and reflective. We aim to provide a language rich environment that is motivating and purposeful.
To support reading and writing the school uses the Tower Hamlets Partnership Phonics Programme (see Phonics section).
Phonic is taught daily across the school, both whole class and streamed.
Phase 1 develops listening skills and awareness of sounds in the environment. In spring term children are introduced to phase 2.
Children are taught phases 2-4 in discrete phonics sessions. By the end of Reception, the children will have been exposed to phase 5 in preparation for year 1.
Revision of phases 2-4 continues. Phase 5 is then taught fully in year 1.
Phase 5 is consolidated and children begin learning more complex grammar and spelling patterns.
Developing a love of reading is the single most powerful attribute that can make a difference to our children’s attainment and enhance their futures.
From the Early Years Foundation Stage, up to Year Two, children here at Elizabeth Selby are encouraged to develop an enjoyment of reading and love of books.
Providing high quality books, children can focus on powerful language, looking at key texts and considering the features of genres. In the Early Years, we teach communication and language, reading and writing through high quality and engaging play based activities.
Two year olds and Nursery
Nursery rhymes and action songs are very much a focus as children begin to develop their communication, language and listening skills. Key texts are also used to link to the termly topics.
In Reception, assessing children’s ability to blend sounds such as c-a-t spells cat, takes place early in the new term.
Using this information, the teacher can plan steps to provide strategies for children to develop skills in being able to read.
The children have daily guided reading sessions where children read in small groups, 1-1 with an adult, individually or whole class with the teacher.
Children revise prior learning and continue to build upon their ability to decode - as in Reception. Guided reading sessions continue daily.
Children progress through colour banded books as they further their skills and apply strategies to become more competent readers.
Colour banded books are taken home, alongside a book of choice to read for pleasure.
Guided Reading continues to takes place daily.
Children use their prior knowledge and a range of skills to become more fluent readers.
We have a range of interventions strategies covering all aspects of reading to support children who may struggle to develop the key skills.
As part of our whole school approach to foster a love of reading, children have a story read to them every day as part of our core values.
Twice a week children take home a book they can independently read and a book of choice that could be read to them at home. They also have a reading diary for parents to comment in.
Children regularly take books home or have books read to them. We communicate with parents though a reading diary. We’ve developed a ‘Snuggle Up and Read’ scheme to encourage parental engagement. Also National events around reading are celebrated with the community. We also have a school library to encourage independent choice of literature.
Through creative and careful planning that factors in challenges, all children have the opportunity to practise and build their confidence in writing.
Two year olds begin their writing journey through early marking making. Children have access to a variety of media to support this.
Nursery provides rich opportunities to mark math both indoors and outdoors, often built around a story or topic they are learning. Children have access to a range of activities that promote both fine and gross motor skills.
The work on fine and gross motor skills continues in Reception. Children continue working on letter formation and using their phonic knowledge, begin to write common words and simple sentences.
The writing journey continues in year 1 with children writing short sentences with punctuation and some accuracy with spelling. They are exposed a range of text from different genres to provide stimulus for writing.
In year 2 children build on prior learning and expand their skills. They begin to write longer pieces paying attention to grammar, hand writing, spelling and punctuation. Children learn to write for a variety of different audiences.
In all year groups Topic based learning is used to enable children to make connections through writing across the curriculum in a creative way.
